title: Stop the Cache Stampede
goal: A flash sale sends 300 requests per second to one product page. Every 5 seconds the cache entry expires and Postgres stalls. Change one file so the database sees about one query per expiry, users stay fast, and price changes still show up.

predict.question: The cache entry for product 42 expires. 300 requests arrive each second, and the summary query takes about 70 ms on an idle database. How many summary queries reach Postgres at that moment?
options: Dozens, and the number grows each cycle
predict.explain: Every request that arrives while the first query runs also sees a miss, so it also queries. Those queries compete for CPU, so each one takes longer, so even more requests miss. That feedback loop is the stampede.

steps.title: Start the lab
steps.text: Starts Postgres, Redis, and the app. The first run downloads images and seeds 2,000,000 reviews.

steps.title: Break it
steps.text: Starts the flash sale. Leave it running.

steps.title: Watch it
steps.text: Run this in a second terminal. Each line is one second: summary queries that reached Postgres, queries running now, and the time for one request.

steps.title: Fix it
steps.text: Edit get_summary(). Then run ./lab restart. Keep break and watch running to see the effect.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Stops your load, runs a clean 40 second flash sale, and checks four rules. A full pass prints a completion code.

rules: Database protected: at most 20 summary queries in 40 seconds (the cache expires about 8 times).
Fast for users: p99 latency at most 300 ms.
No errors: at most 1% of requests fail.
Price change visible: a price update shows within 8 seconds. You cannot cache forever.
hints: Watch the spike in ./lab watch. It comes every 5 seconds. What happens at exactly that moment?
When the key expires, dozens of requests miss at the same time. Only one of them needs to ask the database. What do the others do meanwhile?
asyncio.Lock works inside one process. The app runs 4 processes. Where can all 4 processes share one lock?
Redis SET with nx=True and px=3000 sets a key only if it is missing, with an expiry. The request that gets it refreshes the cache. The others can return an older copy: keep a second key with no TTL.
reflect: Your fix serves slightly old data for a moment. Name one page where that is fine and one where it is not.
The refresher crashes while it holds the lock. What happens, and for how long?
Name another fix that would also pass (hint: refresh before expiry). What does it cost?
